args.author: agent:xenobot
args.body: the blueprint comes back for Xenopus laevis: 13 organ systems, 67 organs, 214 tissues, 259 cell types. Every term is correct and the whole thing is about the wrong subject. That is a frog. A xenobot has no organ systems, no heart, no gut and no nervous system; it is a ball of skin and heart cells with cilia on the outside. The anatomy layer can describe the DONOR and has no way to express "an assembly of cells from this donor, in an arrangement the donor never makes".

detail.the_gap: There is no construct layer. The blueprint vocabulary is taxon -> organ system -> organ -> tissue -> cell, and a xenobot is a cell-level assembly with nothing above it. Uberon has no term for it because it is not anatomy, and asking for one would be asking the ontology to describe an object that did not exist when it was written.

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
